title: DangerZone
wrapsNative: MonarchSectionCard with the danger tone holding androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column rows separated by MonarchDivider; each action is a danger MonarchButton that opens a MonarchDialog
summary: A recipe, not a component: the settings section that holds irreversible actions (delete a workspace, transfer ownership, leave), as a danger-toned section card with one row per action and a confirmation before each.
whenToUse: At the end of a settings screen, for actions that cannot be undone or that hand the workspace or account to someone else.
whenNotToUse: For a single destructive action next to the thing it affects, use a danger MonarchButton with a confirmation (confirm-dialog). For ordinary settings, use the settings-section recipe.
api: MonarchSectionCard(title = "Danger zone", description = …, tone = MonarchTone.Danger) { rows }

Column(Modifier.semantics { isTraversalGroup = true }) { MonarchText(title, style = MonarchTextStyle.BodyStrong, heading = true); MonarchText(consequence, style = MonarchTextStyle.Caption); MonarchText(disabledReason); MonarchButton(…, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Danger, size = MonarchButtonSize.Sm, enabled = …) }

AlertDialog(onDismissRequest = …, title = …, text = …, confirmButton = { MonarchButton(…, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Danger) }, dismissButton = { MonarchButton(…, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Ghost) })

options.name: heading
options.description: The title of the MonarchSectionCard; the danger tone is spoken with it.

options.name: description
options.description: One or two sentences under the heading, such as who can use these actions.

options.name: disabled reason
options.description: Why an action is unavailable: a caption under the consequence, with the action's MonarchButton disabled.

states.name: ready
states.description: Each action is a titled row with its consequence and a danger button under the text.

states.name: unavailable
states.description: The row shows why in a caption and its button is disabled.

states.name: confirming
states.description: The button opens a MonarchDialog with a danger confirm button and Cancel.

states.name: done
states.description: The app reflects the result, for example by disabling the row's button or leaving the screen.

appearance: A MonarchSectionCard with the danger border; item titles are strong body text, consequences and reasons muted captions, actions small danger buttons, rows split by a subtle divider. Every part is an existing component, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web ships DangerZone and DangerZoneItem with heading levels and a layout that places the action beside the text, or under it in a narrow container. On a phone the action always sits under the text, so long titles and font scale 2.0 never squeeze it; MonarchSectionCard already gives the titled card and the danger tone, so Android, like the settings-section recipe, keeps it a recipe. TalkBack has no heading levels, so item titles are headings without a level. The web adds the disabled reason to the row's description; on Android it is a visible caption read in the row's traversal group. Confirmation is a MonarchDialog of the confirm-dialog entry.
accessibility: The card title is a heading and the danger tone is spoken with it, from MonarchSectionCard.
Each item title is a heading, and each row is a traversal group, so the title, consequence, reason and action are read together.
The reason an action is unavailable is visible text, not only a disabled button.
Actions are MonarchButtons with 48dp targets; destructive ones are confirmed in a MonarchDialog that TalkBack focuses.
edgeCases: Keep each consequence to one or two sentences; long text wraps above the button.
After a destructive action succeeds, the app usually leaves the screen; keep the dialog open with a loading confirm button while it runs.
Put the danger zone last on the settings screen.
